title: Impact of Analyst Buy Recommendations on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Event–study analysis.  
Why: An analyst’s buy recommendation is a clearly-timed, idiosyncratic shock to a firm.  The event–study framework isolates the stock-specific abnormal return on (or immediately after) the announcement while purging normal co-movement with the market.

Key identifying assumptions  
1. Market-model validity: E[ε_it | information_t-1]=0, i.e. absent the recommendation the stock’s return would equal α_i + β_i mkt_ret_t.  
2. No confounding events for the same stock on the event day.  
3. Stationary α_i and β_i over the short window we observe.  
If these hold, the abnormal return (AR) on day 0 is the causal effect of the recommendation; its cross-sectional mean is the average treatment effect.

## 2. R Code
```r
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Event-study: impact of analyst BUY recommendations on day-0 CAR
# ------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)

# 1. Load data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s58_data.csv"
dt   <- fread(path)

# 2. Abnormal return using market model  (alpha assumed ≈ 0 over short window)
dt[, ar_mm := ret - beta * mkt_ret]

# 3. One-day CAR (event day 0)
car0 <- dt[event_day == 0]

mean_ar   <- mean(car0$ar_mm, na.rm = TRUE)
se_ar     <- sd(car0$ar_mm,  na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(nrow(car0))
t_stat_ar <- mean_ar / se_ar
p_val_ar  <- 2 * pt(abs(t_stat_ar), df = nrow(car0) - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("=== Main result: market-model abnormal return on day 0 ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Mean AR (%%): %.4f\n", 100*mean_ar))
cat(sprintf("t-stat: %.2f   p-value: %.4f\n\n", t_stat_ar, p_val_ar))

# 4. Robustness check 1: Market-adjusted model (beta = 1, alpha = 0)
dt[, ar_ma := ret - mkt_ret]
car0_ma   <- dt[event_day == 0]
mean_ma   <- mean(car0_ma$ar_ma, na.rm = TRUE)
se_ma     <- sd(car0_ma$ar_ma,  na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(nrow(car0_ma))
t_ma      <- mean_ma / se_ma
p_ma      <- 2 * pt(abs(t_ma), df = nrow(car0_ma) - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("=== Robustness 1: market-adjusted abnormal return on day 0 ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Mean AR (%%): %.4f\n", 100*mean_ma))
cat(sprintf("t-stat: %.2f   p-value: %.4f\n\n", t_ma, p_ma))

# 5. Robustness check 2: Placebo window (pre-event days –5 to –1)
placebo <- dt[event_day %between% c(-5, -1),
              .(placebo_ar = mean(ar_mm, na.rm = TRUE)),
              by = stock_id]
mean_pl  <- mean(placebo$placebo_ar, na.rm = TRUE)
se_pl    <- sd(placebo$placebo_ar,  na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(nrow(placebo))
t_pl     <- mean_pl / se_pl
p_pl     <- 2 * pt(abs(t_pl), df = nrow(placebo) - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("=== Robustness 2: Placebo mean abnormal return (-5 to ‑1) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Mean AR (%%): %.4f\n", 100*mean_pl))
cat(sprintf("t-stat: %.2f   p-value: %.4f\n", t_pl, p_pl))
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Positive abnormal return.  
Magnitude: roughly +1 % (i.e. +0.8 % to +1.5 %) on the event day.

Rationale: A buy recommendation conveys favorable private information or certification, generating immediate optimism and buying pressure.  Prior literature typically finds day-0 abnormal returns between 0.5 % and 2 %.  Because some information may leak and because recommendations can be partially anticipated, the effect is unlikely to exceed ~2 %.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare 1-day CAR before and after the recommendation event.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The analysis suggests a negative impact of analyst buy recommendations on 1-day CAR.
